chapter: Other bands, mutes, arrangers and composers
title: Stock arrangers Frank Skinner, Warrington and Archie Blyer, and why he tricked stocks
summary: DeDroit names his favorite stock arrangers and explains that he altered stocks so his band would not sound like others.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh. Well I guess something else. Did you have any, you sometimes took stocks and tricked them up. Yeah. Did you have any favorite stock, people that did the stock composing, arranging rather?
Yeah, Frank Skinner. Frank Skinner was my favorite.
When was he functioning? He functioned a lot, the time that I, in the forties. In the forties.
Before that were there any that you liked very much? Well they did.

You know the linders in those days were just the voice and the chorus. You know how they wrote them. They didn't have anything but he started tricking them up. There was another one that was very popular with the musicians for some time and he became, on the strength of it, he became a well-known band. I think I know. I can't remember.
But I used to, like I said. Johnny Warrington, did you like him?
Yes, very good. He was very good. You remember Warrington, huh? Yeah, they have a lot of Warrington arrangements here.
Yeah, yeah. He was very good.
He was very good. He was very good. He was very good.
You remember Warrington, huh? Yeah, yeah.
They have a lot of Warrington arrangements here. Yeah, yeah. He was very good. Did you ever play any Archie Blyar arrangements? Yes, very good.

Now you're bringing them back. Archie Blyar was very good. Some of them were a little far out, but after you wait them out, they got all right. You know what I mean? You didn't always have men that could. But the trouble is why I tricked them, I'll tell you why. Because if you put a curtain in front of the bands they all sound alike. You know what I mean? If I played the Stock of the Song from beginning to end of Blue Moon, and that other band plays it, you wouldn't know what band it was then. So I tricked them. Usually because of the fact that we had to play plenty of music, I used to leave out the special things. I used to write modulations, you know, all kinds of fancy modulations.
